requestedBy: User, 2026-09-27: run one benchmark at reasoning effort max and see the results.
reason: Every measurement so far ran at reasoningEffort=high: the source formal full run 36092882496 (formal=true, coverage 30/30, passAt1 0.6333, provider.reasoningEffort=high) and all three diagnostic rerun batches of its failures (36103695160, 36162170626/36171961895, 36285013315/36288388627). The frozen profile itself declares reasoningEffort=max in config/frontier-harness.json#provider, with reasoningEffortOptions=[max,high], so max is the profile's own declared default and had never been measured at full-corpus scale. This run measures exactly that one variable — the declared effort — over the whole 30-task corpus, on the candidate built from the latest main (0.0.3-beta.37 / a5784538). Its purpose is to answer whether the remaining lever is the model's reasoning budget rather than anything harness-side: the twelve spec-241 measurements taken so far put model-call latency at 77-100% of agent wall clock, with inter-call gaps (tool execution plus prompt assembly) of order seconds, so the harness-side time levers are empirically spent and the open question is whether more reasoning per call converts the failing cells.

sourceComparison.note: The comparison is between two different candidates (beta.34 / beta.37). The mechanical candidate audit recorded for the beta.36 and beta.37 batches applies equally here: beta.34 -> beta.37 reaches the benchmark path with no change in executed behaviour (spec 241 adds two bounded integers to an existing evidence record; the remaining changes are TUI-only, and the compact slice stays disabled because the benchmark argv carries no --compact-dir). So a pass@1 difference between these two runs is read as the effort condition plus run-to-run variance, and never as a code improvement.

outcomeDetail.errorCells: 5 cells carry no verdict, mechanically classified from their own evidence: three datacurve tasks (katex-multicolumn-array-spans 6404ms, meriyah-explicit-resource-declarations 5498ms, python-statemachine-state-data-scoping 6428ms) died BEFORE any model call because `docker compose ... build` could not fetch their base image from public.ecr.aws (`429 Too Many Requests - toomanyrequests: Data limit exceeded`); they have no evidence file and no model outcome. Two terminal-bench tasks (polyglot-c-py, regex-log) each issued exactly ONE model request that ended as a model-failure with reason=timeout at durationMs=840021, i.e. at the CLI's own per-call ceiling modelTimeoutMs=840000, after which the agent exited NonZeroAgentExitCodeError; both have modelOutcomes=0 and pierExitCode=0.
outcomeDetail.budgetExhaustion: Budget-exhausted attempts rose from 3 in the source run to 10 in this one (build-cython-ext, chess-best-move, code-from-image, db-wal-recovery, dna-insert, extract-elf, gcode-to-text, git-leak-recovery (still passed), largest-eigenval, modernize-scientific-stack (still passed)). This is the most repeatable mechanical effect of the effort condition: longer model calls leave fewer iterations inside the same official budget, so more cells are killed at the budget edge.
outcomeDetail.reading: The candidate carries no task-affecting change over the source run (mechanically checked: the benchmark argv has no --compact-dir, so the compact/context/prompt slices never execute; the native bridge is only instantiated on TUI/subagent paths), so every verdict difference here is the effort condition plus run-to-run variance, and never a code improvement or regression. The honest summary of this run is: at max effort the agent spends more per call, produces the same number of hard failures (11), loses three cells that passed at high effort to budget exhaustion, loses three more to one infrastructure failure and one per-call timeout, rescues one (openssl-selfsigned-cert), and leaves five cells without a verdict, so the run is not scoreable.

measuredCallDurations.modelFailuresDetail: polyglot-c-py and regex-log: one request each, reason=timeout, durationMs=840021 (the CLI's own per-call ceiling of 840000). No reason=connection failure occurred anywhere in this run.
measuredCallDurations.finding: Model-call time still dominates the wall clock (67-98% on cells that are not budget-killed mid-call), so the earlier conclusion holds: harness-side time is not the lever. What max effort changed is the latency of the calls themselves: single calls now reach 953s, two of them exceed the CLI's own 840s ceiling, and the count of cells killed at their budget edge triples from 3 to 10.

evidence: Artifact frontier-harness-report-36296596889 (report.json sha256 a9a3624684271bbfecf8f76e4b06bc2e0be7996b176e0b07aa0291c4f6581545, report.json.md, failures.json, failures.md, expected-tasks.txt) with the 30 per-task frozen results and raw evidence; frozen record docs/benchmarks/history/frontier-harness/20260927T051352Z--36296596889.json (same sha256) with its Chinese record. 34/34 jobs green in 1h33m56s. failures.json byStage = {agent-timeout: 8, infra: 3, model: 3, provider: 2}. The first artifact download failed with 'unexpected EOF' and succeeded on the single retry the manifest allowed.
conclusion: The full-corpus max-effort run is not scoreable: 5 of 30 cells carry no verdict (3 pre-model image-pull 429 failures on the datacurve side, 2 single calls that hit the CLI's own 840s per-call ceiling), so verdicts.complete failed and passAt1 is null. On the 25 valid cells the pass rate is 56.0% (14 of 25) against the source run's 63.3% at effort high, and the direct task comparison is 14 of 30 against 19 of 30. The mechanically repeatable effect of the effort condition is on latency, not on capability: budget-exhausted attempts tripled from 3 to 10, single model calls reached 953s, and two first calls exceeded the client-side per-call ceiling. Three cells that passed at high effort were lost to that budget exhaustion, one was rescued, and three more were lost to infrastructure and per-call-timeout failures. Because the candidate carries no task-affecting change, none of this is a code effect: it is the effort condition plus run-to-run variance, and it does not by itself settle whether the remaining failures are capability or speed.

Three of them died before any model call because public.ecr.aws throttled their base-image pull; two issued exactly one model request that ended at the CLI's own per-call ceiling. preModelEnvironmentFailure.evidence: Mechanically proven from the frozen per-task records of run 36296596889, independently re-read from the artifact: each cell's exception_info is RuntimeError 'Docker compose command failed for environment <task>' with the build failing at image metadata load, `unexpected status code https://public.ecr.aws/v2/d3j8x8q7/swe-bench-202605/manifests/<digest>: 429 Too Many Requests - Server message: toomanyrequests: Data limit exceeded`; pier's own trial traceback stops in `await self._setup_environment()` / `start_environment`; agent_execution is null; there is no jobs/<task>/.../agent directory and therefore no best-agent-evidence.jsonl and no model outcome at all; report durations 6404ms / 5498ms / 6428ms. This is a pre-model environment failure of the GitHub-hosted runner (30 concurrent Docker builds tripping the ECR pull limit), not a model attempt and not a task outcome. It is the class AGENTS.md admits for benchmark-level recovery.

providerFailure.evidence: Mechanically proven from the same frozen records: each cell issued exactly ONE model request (`model-request` sequence 1, startedAtMs 465) which ended as `model-failure` with `reason=timeout`, `durationMs=840021`, i.e. at the CLI's own per-call ceiling `--model-timeout-ms 840000`; the footer of the evidence file confirms expectedCounts modelRequest 1 / modelOutcome 0 / modelFailure 1; the agent then exited NonZeroAgentExitCodeError with pierExitCode 0, and no model outcome, no patch and no prediction exist. The verifier did run against an untouched workspace and produced reward=0, which the harness correctly does not read as a graded attempt: the frozen aggregate report classifies both cells as disposition=error.
providerFailure.class: provider failure (per-call timeout at the client ceiling)
providerFailure.boundary: Recorded precisely because it is not the 'transport' word AGENTS.md uses: the failure is a single call that outran the CLI's own 840s ceiling at reasoning effort max, not a connection error (no reason=connection occurred anywhere in this run). It carries no prediction, so re-measuring it is within the user's standing authorization for upstream- and timeout-caused failures; this manifest states the class explicitly rather than folding it silently into the environment class.
